While observing a sunday School ceremony for African-American children, this man asked if the children had any message for their white counterparts, to which someone stood up and said "Tell them we are rising." John de Grey and Reginald vied for this post after one holder died, but neither was selected. Name this city, the capital of Bengal, home to an infamous 1756 "black hole."

A. W. Singham argued that this organization has become focused on international economic reform, highlighting the differences in ideology between its resource-rich and resource-poor members. One militia which fought in this battle was originally employed for foraging, although the winning commander threatened to demote their officers when they did not obey his order to parade because they were busy foraging. This council was reconvened by the papal bull "Ad ecclesiae regimen." One of the most influential speakers at this council was Diego Laynez. Because of superstition, this entity did not hold meetings more than a mile outside of the pomerium. Plebians who were forced into being conscripti became a part of it. During this event, helicopters dumped huge quantities of boron, sand and lead onto a burning building because reacting water with graphite produces carbon monoxide. Genetic defects induced by caesium-137 and strontium-90 have been caused due to this disaster. Name this nuclear disaster that occurred in the Ukraine.

Name this modern-day capital of Iraq.

One ruler with this name reversed the liberal trends of his father by following what he outlined in the Accession Manifesto and was known as "the Peasants' Tsar." Foreign Minister Jan Masaryk's mysterious death here was declared to be accidental by the government of Alexander Dubcek in this city's namesake spring. Name this capital of Czechoslovakia.

Identify this office held by Nasser, Sadat, and recently-ousted scumbag Hosni Mubarak, whose offices are located in Cairo.

This ruler captured Theobald I after invading Lorraine in support of Philip Augustus during the War of Succession of Champagne. The "Old Lord of Beiruit" opposed the forces of this man, who used his fluency in Arabic to negotiate a controversial treaty with the Ayyubid Al-Kamil which left this man as King of Jerusalem and plunged the Crusader States into the War of the Lombards. Pietro della Vigna figured in his court's cultural efforts, which centrally involved his son Enzio of Sardinia's kingdom in Sicily. The Treaty of San Germano lifted one of Gregory IX's several excommunications of this ruler, who confirmed Teutonic Knight holdings in Prussia in the Golden Bull of Rimini. A failed siege of Parma ended the dominance of this ruler, which began after his uncle Otto IV of Brunswick lost at Bouvines. Identify this last great Hohenstaufen Holy Roman Emperor, the second of his name after a grandfather known as "Barbarossa."

This leader's treasurer, Catalina Villalpando, was convicted of tax evasion. His appointment of William Reilly to another position drew environmentalists' praise. This man claimed to have "Big Mo" on his side during his first presidential run. He repeatedly checked his watch during the second debate in his re-election campaign. After UN Security Council Resolution 794, this President launched Operation Restore Hope to give aid in Africa. He supported Guillermo Endara in Operation Just Cause, which ousted Manuel Noriega. Name this deliverer of the "thousand points of light" speech, who appointed Supreme Court Justices David Souter and Clarence Thomas after running the "Willie Horton" ad to defeat Michael Dukakis and become the 41st president of the United States.

This man hung spoils of honor on an oak tree after slaying a king of Caenina named Acron. In one story, he vanished after a storm cloud on the Goats' Marsh enveloped him. He avoided fighting the Antemnates after pleas from Hersilia, his wife. One traitor to this man asked for the bracelets on enemy soldiers' left arms; that woman, who was crushed by shields instead, was Tarpeia. This leader cursed all men who tried to leap over his low walls. This grandson of Numitor hosted a festival of Neptune attended by Titus Tatius's people, at which he authorized kidnappings. He was succeeded by Numa Pompilius, became the god Quirinus after death, and staked one claim after seeing twelve birds fly by. Name this legendarily wolf-suckled founder who killed his brother Remus before founding Rome.

By signing one treaty in this city, the Kingdom of Yugoslavia agreed to let a neighbor annex the Free State of Fiume. A meeting at Val Duchesse preceded one treaty which six countries signed in this city at the same time as the Euratom treaty. Another agreement signed in this city entered force in 2002 and set up The Hague as the location for the International Criminal Court. An earlier treaty named for this city was signed by the Benelux countries, France, Italy, and West Germany; that treaty, which turned the ECSC into the European Economic Community, was later modified by the treaties of Lisbon and Maastricht to create the EU. Name this large European city where the Lateran Treaty was signed to distinguish it from its enclave of Vatican City.

Lauzun's Legion unhorsed an enemy commander at this battle before the Marquis de Choisy withdrew them. A 150-person fort at this battle's northern end contained the 23rd Welch Fusiliers. A storm ruined the eventual losers' plans to evacuate to Gloucester Point. Thomas Nelson allegedly had its winners fire at the enemy general's quarters in Nelson's own home. Robert Abercromby's night raid at this battle spiked six cannons that all got repaired by morning. Charles O'Hara presented a sword to the winners of this battle that followed the Comte de Grasse's naval victory over Thomas Graves. Decided after the capture of redoubts Nine and Ten, name this 1781 battle at which the Comte de Rochambeau, Lafayette, and Washington accepted Cornwallis's surrender to win the American Revolution.

A 2.5 percent income tax was levied to fund this conflict by the letter Graves orientalis terrae. This war was chronicled at the time by Geoffrey of Villehardouin. Fulk of Neuilly preached in favor of going to this war. Up to two-thirds of its intended army defected in the year after the siege of a port city under Emeric of Hungary's control called Zadar or Zara. Though Boniface of Montferrat led its troops, Baldwin of Flanders was crowned Latin Emperor in its aftermath. Offers from Alexius IV Angelus moved its intended target from Alexandria after the blind doge Enrico Dandolo sought to regain debt through it and let its fleet sail from Venice. Name this campaign called by Innocent III, a crusade which included a sack of Constantinople in 1204 AD.

A Brian Vaughan graphic novel about this war spread the story of four lions who escaped from a zoo during it, only to be shot. During this war, locals used earthmoving equipment to break dykes and reflood dried reed marshes, and troops occupied a resort called Dreamland for one siege, after which generals denied their use of white phosphorous shells as incendiary weapons. For two years, Ray Odierno commanded this war's multi-national force. A president spoke about it aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln a month before the capture of the so-called "ace of diamonds." After the fedayeen fell, this war involved the setup of a "Green Zone" in a captured capital and the ambush of four contractors in Fallujah. Name this war and insurgency begun in 2003, in which the US ousted Saddam Hussein.

During debate over an amendment proposed by this man, Senator Edmunds of Vermont ordered the Syllabus of Errors to be read aloud. A resolution offered by this man, in which he quoted the 14th Amendment, became the focus of the Teller Committee on post-Reconstruction voting in the South. He tried to mollify the American response to the USS Baltimore incident using contacts he made as chair of the first Pan-American Conference. This author of the Mulligan Letters was tarnished when the New York World reported a sermon from Samuel Burchard about the "Rum, Romanism, and Rebellion" of his opponent. Name this Secretary of State under Benjamin Harrison, a Speaker of the House and failed 1884 presidential candidate called the "Continental Liar from the State of Maine."

This civilization's leaders appointed seven, then eight, honorary bodyguards. One of its leaders' remains are stored in a golden box decorated with a sixteen-pointed sun emblem. This civilization once used a nine-story high siege tower with sloped walls, whose iron plating was later melted down for use in statuary. Its military used eight divisions of spear-bearing "Companion cavalry." The battle of Pydna was a loss for this kingdom's ruler Perseus after it had suffered earlier loss at Cynoscephalae to Rome during its Antigonid dynasty. Earlier, this empire, which pioneered the use of an extra-long pike known as the sarissa, was attacked in speeches by Demosthenes. Name this ancient Greek empire whose phalanxes were commanded by kings such as Philip II and his son, Alexander the Great.

This man vocally criticized the parceling of land in the Kakamega Reserve to gold miners. Recent evidence suggests that he ordered the death of cabinet minister C.M.G. Argwings-Kodhek. His widow Mama Ngina and other members of his family smuggled tons of ivory into China. This man politically opposed his son Peter Muigai during a time period including Operation Anvil. After Governor Baring declared a state of emergency, this man was arrested during Operation Jock Scott and tried at Kapenguria while Dedan Kimathi fled. He headed the KANU party after his release and wrote a thesis defending female genital mutilation with an introduction by Bronislaw Malinowski. Name this figure succeeded by Daniel arap Moi who, after the Mau Mau Rebellion, was the first president of Kenya.

Johann Burchard wrote an account of events held by this ruler called the Liber Notarum. This man was the second leader in his highest post to accept money in order to shelter Prince Djem, an exiled brother of Bayezid II. One of his sons became prince of Squillace. One of his rivals fled to Ostia to hide from him; that rival, Giuliano della Rovere, invited Charles VIII of France to invade Italy. This alleged holder of the super-sexual "banquet of chestnuts" issued the decree Inter caetera among his Bulls of Donation, which established a demarcation line. This man had his zealous rival Savonarola excommunicated and executed. Name this corrupt father of Lucrezia and a son extolled by Machiavelli named Cesare, who from 1492 to 1503 served as the second Borgia pope.

Sir Matthew Nathan refused to pre-emptively arrest the leaders of this event after the capture of the Aud, citing a lack of authority. Lord Wimborne was consequently forced to declare martial law. Roger Casement was executed for treason for trying to secure weapons from Germany to support this effort. Due to sniper fire from the Shelbourne hotel during it, forces under Michael Mallin were unable to hold St. Stephen's Green. The rebels during this event, who issued the Proclamation of the Republic, were headquartered in the General Post Office and were led by the head of the "Citizen Army", James Connolly, and by Patrick Pearse. Eamon de Valera was one of the few major rebel survivors of, what 1916 failed Irish rebellion against British rule, named for the holiday on which it occurred?

A 2010 Stan Richardson play was based on a file exposing this place's Secret Court, which was formed after Cyril Wilcox's 1920 suicide and cast out ten of the people that this place spied on for suspected "homosexualism." The compiler of the "Five-Foot Shelf" of books, Charles W. Eliot, de-Christianized and transformed this place over four decades in a position held earlier by Edward Everett and Increase Mather. Harry Starr fought the Jewish quota in this institution, which merged with all-female Radcliffe College in 1977. Unkind comments on natural female intelligence led Lawrence Summers to resign its presidency in 2006. Name this institution with freshman residences surrounding a namesake Yard, founded in 1636 in Cambridge, Massachusetts as America's first college.

One side in this war used the town of Erbessus as a quickly-captured supply dump. During this war, Boodes captured a first-time naval commander. Its losers refused riotously harsh peace terms after a rout at Adys; those terms came from this war's winning general at Cape Ecnomus, the eventual prisoner Marcus Atilius Regulus. As recorded in the first of forty books in Polybius's Histories, this war's winners used a device called the raven, or corvus, to board enemy ships at Mylae. It began when the Mamertines asked both sides for aid against Hiero II, while the losers fought their own mercenaries afterwards. The truce ending this war broke with the siege of Saguntum. Name this war fought mainly in Sicily that made Hamilcar Barca's name, in which Rome first fought its southerly rival Carthage.

These people won the Battle of the Nobles in a great revolt nineteen years after unfair tattooing led bodyguards of this ethnicity to kill their master. A female soothsayer of this people, who ordered the destruction of their own property to avert enemy attacks, was called the Kahina. The dynasties of these people included the Zirid client state. A man named Kusaila led the Sanhaja group of them against Uqba ibn-Naf. A subset of them fought against Francisco Franco in the second Rif War. The Strait of Gibraltar is named for a military commander of this ethnic group. They include the nomadic Tuaregs. Historical ones inhabited and led the Almohad and Almoravid empires in the Maghreb and southern Spain. Name these people who adopted Islam from the Arabs and who inhabit North Africa.

One ruler of this dynasty was buried with three hundred golden insects and a golden bull's head. The Rauching conspiracy threatened a ruler of this dynasty, during which the Battle of Tertry was a loss for the Neustrian army. According to Fredegar, its founder was sired by a half-fish, half-bull monster with five horns. An early leader of this dynasty defeated the Alemanni at Tolbiac and won at Soissons against Syagrius, an ex-Roman general, as told by Gregory of Tours. These kings all had long hair and gave power to regional "mayors of the palace" after Dagobert I's rule. The papacy deposed its last ruler, Childeric III. An earlier queen of this dynasty, Clotilde, affected a Catholic conversion in its uniting conqueror, Clovis. Name this Frankish dynasty preceding the Carolingians.
